newsitem.title: FRANCE: French neo-Nazis go on trial for graveyard outrage.
newsitem.headline: French neo-Nazis go on trial for graveyard outrage.

text.p: Four French neo-Nazis go on trial on Monday for a 1990 anti-Semitic graveyard outrage which caused nationwide revulsion and prompted a protest march by hundreds of thousands led by the late President Francois Mitterrand.

Yannick Garnier, 27, Patrick Laonegro, 31, Bertrand Nouveau, 28, and Olivier Fimbry, also 28, are accused of unearthing the recently buried body of Felix Germon in a Jewish cemetery, placing graveyard emblems on his corpse and simulating his sodomisation with a beach umbrella.
They face two-year prison sentences each.

They were only arrested last July when Garnier, once a skinhead but who had since settled down and found a job, gave himself up to police, reportedly because his conscience troubled him. He identified the others.
Police said they found Nazi magazines, videotapes and similar objects, including a bust of Adolf Hitler, in the homes of those involved.
All confessed but said the operation was the idea of Jean-Claude Gos, since killed in a motorcycle accident and who they say threatened to kill them if they spoke about it.

The discovery of Germon's unearthed body in the centuries-old Jewish cemetery at Carpentras in southern France caused protests across France with the then-President Mitterrand leading a huge march across Paris.

Mitterrand's Interior Minister Pierre Joxe visited the cemetery within hours and said the "guilty were known," adding that the outrage resulted from "the anti-Semitic speeches of (extreme rightist leader) Jean-Marie Le Pen."

Le Pen protested his innocence and complained that he was victim of a witchhunt. For years until the accused were arrested, publications close to his National Front (NF) party spoke of "police provocations." None of the accused are FN members.
Police questioned many ulta-rightists in months that followed the outrage including two of those now on trial, both of whom then presented credible alibis.
